question: A subset $u_1,u_2,u_3,u_4,u_5$ of the first $90$ positive integers can be selected in $\binom{90}{5}$ ways. Let $u_{\max}=\max\{u_1,u_2,u_3,u_4,u_5\}$ and $u_{\min}=\min\{u_1,u_2,u_3,u_4,u_5\}$. Then the arithmetic mean of $u_{\max}+u_{\min}$ over all such subsets is
solution:
Counting subsets according to their maximum and minimum and applying the hockey-stick identity gives
\[
\sum(u_{\max}+u_{\min})=91\binom{90}{5}.
\]
Dividing by $\binom{90}{5}$ gives the arithmetic mean $91$.
